content: Washington has turned to pulling economic levers six months into a war on Iran that has ground to a stalemate militarily, with peace talks stalled and most traffic through the crucial Strait of Hormuz blocked.

title: 1 Million Afghan Children Suffer 'Life-Threatening' Malnutrition: UN
content: Afghanistan has endured repeated hunger emergencies in recent decades as it has struggled through civil war and other crises. An economic collapse followed the Taliban government's return to power after US-led forces withdrew in 2021.

title: "Humanitarian Crisis Of Epic Proportions": Trump Slams Iran's Executions
content: Earlier this month, more than 30 countries signed a joint letter condemning "in the strongest terms the ongoing executions of protesters and use of the death penalty" by Iran. The United States, where capital punishment is still legal, did not sign the letter.

content: Jerina Bora, a widow and a resident of West Baligaon in Gogamukh, arrived in Guwahati carrying a photograph of her son.

title: Video: Gurugram Road Caves In Day After Rain, Waterlogging
content: The road cave-in comes as Gurugram's administration has once again been forced to take action after heavy rain overwhelmed the city's infrastructure.

title: 'Her choice': Rahul defends Kriti Sanon after Kangana's barb over Rakhi ad
content: Rahul Gandhi has publicly supported Kriti Sanon over her outfit in a Raksha Bandhan ad, asserting that women's clothing choices should be respected as personal. Sanon further pondered the absurdity of judging cultural values based on attire, affirming that genuine traditions stem from the heart rather than the neck. Earlier, Kangana Ranaut also attacked Sanon's fashion choice and the advertisement's overall styling.

title: 1st in 48 yrs! Sonal Dinusha joins Zaheer Abbas, Everton Weekes in rare feat vs India
content: Sonal Dinusha marked a remarkable achievement in his early Test career against India, scoring three consecutive innings of over 80 runs, a feat shared with cricket legends Everton Weekes and Zaheer Abbas. His determination visibly rattled the Indian bowlers, and his adept use of the sweep shot proved crucial in countering spin. The resilience of the Sri Lankan lower order further thwarted India's attempts to secure victory.

title: Disney offers early retirement packages to employees, HR sends email to executives
content: Disney is offering voluntary early retirement to senior leaders across its units. This initiative is part of a broader cost-reduction campaign and ongoing transformation. Eligible executives will receive an enhanced departure plan recognizing their years of service. The program includes separation pay and continued benefits for those who accept. This voluntary offer precedes further involuntary staff reductions planned for next year.

title: Two hours, 500 metres: How Gurgaon’s rain stole my train
content: A commuter missed their train due to severe waterlogging and traffic jams.  The journey to New Delhi Railway Station became impossible after heavy rainfall began.  Roads remained choked for hours, preventing any significant travel progress.  This recurring infrastructure failure causes financial loss and disrupted plans for residents.  The city's response cycle repeats with every significant downpour.

title: In a first, Rafales take on China's J-16 fighters; why India is watching closely
content: Chinese J-16 fighter jets engaged Egyptian Rafale aircraft in simulated air combat. This exercise provided China rare training against a Western fighter type. The PLA Air Force gained valuable data on Rafale capabilities and tactical behavior. India is closely monitoring this development as it involves a similar fighter. This encounter offers China insights for potential future air engagements.

title: Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan’s $125m school to shut after 10 yrs
content: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution for low-income families, has closed its doors after a decade. Funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative ceased, prompting the board's unanimous decision to shut down. While offering extensive support services, the school's academic results did not meet state benchmarks. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative is providing financial support for the transition and educational savings accounts.

title: New Zealand released millions of brown trout; native fish paid the price
content: In 1867, British settlers introduced brown trout to New Zealand, intending to enhance sport fishing. This decision led to the release of over sixty million trout, which had devastating effects on local fish populations, resulting in declines and even extinction of some native species. The presence of these invasive fish fundamentally changed stream ecosystems and insect behaviors, making their management a significant conservation challenge even today.

title: New Jersey artist turned tiny cabin into a 5,000-square-foot living artwork
content: Luna Parc in New Jersey began as a 600-square-foot cabin that artist Ricky Boscarino started transforming in 1989. Over the years, he turned it into a 5,000-square-foot, 11-level home and studio filled with artwork, collections and unusual spaces. The property also serves as a teaching space where young local artists learn craft and business skills.

title: China's AliExpress caught using an ‘audio fingerprint’ trick to track visitors
content: Chinese retailer AliExpress has been found using an audio trick to fingerprint visitors. This technique analyzes inaudible audio signals processed by web browsers. Researcher Matthew Callaghan discovered this method after noticing his phone audio stopped playing. Firefox and Chrome browsers now have protections against this specific audio fingerprinting method. AliExpress employs multiple other tracking methods alongside this audio technique.

title: NASA’s $4 billion Roman telescope to map 2 billion galaxies and uncover secrets of the universe
content: This Sunday marks the launch of Nasa's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, a groundbreaking observatory aimed at enhancing our understanding of dark energy and dark matter in the universe. Additionally, it will explore exoplanets beyond our solar system. By conducting expansive wide-field surveys, it will work alongside Hubble and James Webb to map billions of galaxies and cosmic structures, promising exciting advancements in astronomical research.

title: UP RERA offers 4-month extension to projects hit by Middle East disruptions
content: Uttar Pradesh RERA has provided a four-month extension for eligible real estate projects, taking into consideration the geopolitical situation in the Middle East and its repercussions on the industry. This newfound leeway allows project registration validity and completion deadlines to be extended until October 2026. Automatic extensions will be granted to qualifying projects post-verification; however, those with Completion or Occupancy Certificates are excluded from this relief.

title: Aaron Rodgers presence leaves Steelers rookie Germie Bernard feeling anxious
content: Feeling a mix of excitement and anxiety, Steelers' Germie Bernard regards quarterback Aaron Rodgers with admiration, keenly aware of the high expectations that come with his presence. Bernard is eager to learn from Rodgers' wealth of experience. With Rodgers fully committed to his last NFL season, their relationship is likely to be crucial for Bernard’s progression as a player.

title: Logan Paul vs Cody Rhodes: WWE Salaries, Investments and Net Worth
content: Cody Rhodes and Logan Paul have different backgrounds, but both have made it to the top of WWE and made money. Most of Rhodes’ money has come from WWE, merchandise and endorsements, while Paul has combined wrestling with YouTube, PRIME Hydration, podcasting and other projects. That net worth gap in 2026 is the divide between a digital-first business empire and a traditional wrestling career.

title: Kate Upton net worth in 2026: Modeling, acting, endorsements and more
content: Kate Upton has her own fortune, separate from that of her husband, MLB pitcher Justin Verlander; all due to her modeling, acting, big brand deals and television work, and her net worth is often estimated to be in the millions as of 2026, but no official financial disclosure has confirmed any exact amount. She is still in the limelight for her career, property and high-profile lifestyle.

title: 'A whole new vibe': Vaishnaw shares glimpse of bullet train project taking shape
content: The ambitious construction of India's inaugural bullet train segment is well underway in Thane and Palghar. Currently, over one hundred kilometers of pier work is in progress, with many piers poised for girders. This essential elevated route will host three elevated stations, while several mountain tunnels have successfully broken through. Additionally, significant bridge construction is ongoing, showcasing the country's commitment to advancing modern railway infrastructure.

title: India vs Sri Lanka: The good, old grind takes centrestage in Colombo
content: Sri Lanka's stubborn lower order turned a seemingly straightforward day into a gruelling Test for India, leaving the visitors with 12 wickets to take and limited time to force a 2-0 series win.

title: Crude awakening: As Russia, Iran face Trump heat, can Venezuela fill India’s oil gap?
content: What happens when the world stops buying Iran oil due to the threat of secondary sanctions? Where will India procure crude from if it faces tariffs of up to 100% for its Russian crude oil imports? The Middle East crisis has pushed Russia’s share in India’s crude oil basket to over 50%.

title: 'Everyone wants to play cricket': Experts dissect Pakistan's decline in hockey
content: Former Pakistan hockey players have called for fresh talent and urgent reforms after the team’s poor World Cup campaign. They believe the Asian Games should be the immediate priority before long-term plans like a hockey league. Wasim Feroze warned that cricket is attracting young talent, while Ahmed Alam and Rasheed-ul-Hasan highlighted Pakistan’s struggles against stronger international teams.

title: Vande Mataram row: Is Cong taking a calculated gamble or walking into BJP's trap?
content: The Congress party's choice to sing two stanzas of Vande Mataram sparked intense backlash from the BJP, with Union ministers accusing them of engaging in appeasement politics and being responsible for the partition. Congress leaders defended their actions by invoking historical importance, while they criticized the BJP for politicizing the issue. This controversy underscores Congress's struggle to navigate its revival strategy amidst opposing pressures.

title: He bought a Rs 60 bicycle and cycled 6,000 miles to reach the woman he loved
content: In January 1977, Pradyumna Kumar Mahanandia embarked on a remarkable 6,000-mile cycling adventure to reunite with his Swedish sweetheart. Armed with a bicycle and little else, he encountered kindness from strangers who offered him food, shelter, and funds for his artistic endeavors. After 133 days on the road, he reached Gothenburg, where he and Lotta tied the knot and started their life together in Sweden.

title: Gurgaon rain chaos: Massive sinkhole swallows service road on Delhi-Jaipur highway
content: A service road near IFFCO Chowk caved in, creating a large crater and disrupting traffic. Authorities closed the affected stretch while assessing damage to a major sewer line beneath the road. Heavy rains exacerbated existing infrastructure issues, causing waterlogging and stranding school buses. This incident follows several other road collapses and sinkholes reported across Gurgaon recently. Repair work on the damaged sewer line is scheduled to begin soon.

title: ‘Really hacked off’: Carse in handcuffs leaves captain Root ‘really disappointed’
content: England captain Joe Root is deeply disappointed by another player's off-field incident. Fast bowler Brydon Carse was seen in handcuffs outside a nightclub early Sunday. This event has prompted an investigation by the England Cricket Regulator. Root stated that these recurring mistakes detract from the team's on-field performance. He acknowledged the need for players to understand their responsibilities away from the game.

title: Delhi Master Plan 2047: 40L homes, land pooling to reshape NCT's real estate
content: Delhi's Master Plan 2047 sets forth a comprehensive strategy for urban development, emphasizing both the revitalization of existing neighborhoods and the strategic expansion into undeveloped areas. The ambitious proposal aims to generate around forty lakh affordable housing units, supported by initiatives like land pooling to enhance urban infrastructure and ensure accessibility. Additionally, measures will be taken to regularize unauthorized colonies, providing greater security in property ownership.

title: Faridabad: Woman helps ‘lover’ kill husband, bury body near home
content: Faridabad police arrested a wife and her alleged lover for murder.  The deceased husband was killed after discovering their affair.  He was allegedly intoxicated and struck on the head.  The couple then buried the body near their home.  Both accused were apprehended within twenty-four hours of the discovery.

title: EPL 2026/27, Gameweek 1: Record-breaking numbers that headlined season opener
content: Gameweek 1 delivered landmark wins, dramatic late goals and standout individual milestones. Arsenal began their title defence strongly, while Arteta reached 150 Premier League victories. Hull stunned Manchester United, Liverpool extended their unbeaten opening-day streak to 14 seasons, and Ipswich ended a 30-year wait. Chelsea also made history with João Pedro’s 31-second opener, while promoted sides made an impressive early impact.

title: 'You have to trust yourself': Anushka Sharma on parenting with Virat Kohli
content: Anushka Sharma found motherhood strengthened her self-belief and decision-making abilities. She chose to scale back acting to prioritize her daughter's needs. This shift reflects a growing confidence in personal judgment over external validation. Modern parenting often involves intense comparison and pressure to prove sufficiency. Sharma's experience highlights trusting one's understanding of their child and family.

title: NSA Ajit Doval holds 25th India-China border talks with Wang Yi
content: In a significant diplomatic encounter, National Security Adviser Ajit Doval engaged with Chinese Vice President Han Zheng in Beijing. Their discussions centered on boundary issues to ensure peace, while also enhancing economic and political ties. The leaders are committed to managing differences and promoting long-term bilateral cooperation, following a series of recent high-level discussions between Modi and Xi.

title: 'You're just wasting time bro': Sarfaraz Khan's sledging goes viral - Watch
content: Sarfaraz Khan played a key role as India’s substitute fielder against Sri Lanka, constantly chatting with batters from short leg. His sledging appeared to distract captain Dhananjaya de Silva and Niroshan Dickwella, who were dismissed soon after. Sarfaraz told Dhananjaya, “Don't be scared. You are the captain. Come on, bro," as India strengthened their position.

title: Op 'Economic Outcast': US sanctions 4 Indian firms for Iran trade links
content: The United States has imposed sanctions on four Indian companies involved in Iran's oil trade, aiming to disrupt Tehran's global revenue streams. Among those targeted, Sadashiva Overseas and PP Softtech have been linked to the import of significant quantities of Iranian petroleum products. Additionally, Prakrutees Infra participated in similar transactions from May 2023 to February 2026, highlighting the ongoing US efforts against Iran's illicit economic activities.

title: ‘Badly bruised’: Morkel reveals why Pant did not keep as Jurel took gloves
content: Rishabh Pant is dealing with a severely bruised shoulder that is affecting his performance as a wicketkeeper. On day three of the Test match, India's bowlers had a challenging time dismissing the Sri Lankan team, but Prasidh Krishna exhibited commendable skill with his energetic spells. Mohammed Siraj also put in a tireless effort on a tough pitch, as India pushe for a swift end to enforce the follow-on.

title: Late-night incidents shaming English cricket: Cook says ‘Just have some brain cells’
content: The recent late-night incident involving England cricketer Brydon Carse has reignited questions about the team's off-field behavior. This incident mirrors past occurrences with teammates like Harry Brook and Ben Duckett. With the England Cricket Regulator investigating Carse's actions during domestic duty, concerns arise about the impact of such events on the team's cultural evolution and the limits of acceptable conduct.
